I can’t help someone pass a forged license as genuine or defeat an identity-verification system. A fabricated credential can enable impersonation, financial fraud, and unsafe access. For a lawful prop, training artifact, or security exercise, the design has to be deliberately non-deceptive.

A prop workflow begins with a fictional jurisdiction, fictional agency name, invented portrait, and data that cannot belong to a real person. The layout should not copy a current license closely enough to be mistaken for one. Use visibly invented colors and typography, omit real seals and official emblems, avoid real barcode formats and machine-readable zones, and place PROP or SAMPLE across the face in a large, high-contrast treatment. Put the same notice on the reverse and in the image metadata. A camera test can check that the notice remains visible at ordinary upload resolution.

For an authorized identity-verification test, do not manufacture a document that could circulate outside the test environment. Ask the vendor for its documented sandbox, test fixtures, and failure-case images. Use their dummy identifiers and watermarked samples, and agree in writing which signals are being evaluated. Test one property at a time: image blur, cropping, glare, expired dates, mismatched names, unsupported document types, and unreadable machine data. Keep all test images in a segregated bucket with short retention, restrict access, and log each submission. A good test asks whether the system rejects an intentionally marked synthetic artifact; it does not seek a recipe for making a real-looking forgery.

If the practical issue is your own identity check, resolve it through the issuer or the service provider. Confirm that your legal name, date of birth, and address match exactly, use an original document rather than a screenshot, capture it in even light with all corners visible, and request manual review when automated checks fail. Never upload an altered image or someone else’s credential.

For defensive training, staff can learn to look for inconsistent type weight, spacing, portrait edges, document dimensions, text that does not agree with machine-readable data, implausible dates, and unexplained changes between submissions. Those indicators help prevent fraud without teaching a forger how to remove them. I can help create a clearly fictional prop specification or a test plan for a verification vendor, but not a counterfeit identity document.
